Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words. At Home is the state every buyer is trying to reach, named in the simplest English available. The brand sits on the destination, not the transaction. Plain, warm, immediately legible.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern real estate has been moving from agent-led to platform-led, with the customer doing more of the discovery work themselves. The opening is for a brand that respects the buyer as a design-literate adult and treats the agent as a real, accountable person.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Compass (compass.com) holds the modern tech-led peer position. Side (side.com) sits in the agent-platform tier. Zillow (zillow.com) does the consumer marketplace middle. We sit closer to Side in posture, with a sharper consumer brand.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern brokerage with named agents, clean listings, and no broker speak.

Modern.tagline: A brokerage for the long calendar.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words that say the quiet part out loud — most clients are not buying now, they are buying later. We made the timeline the name. It signals patience, slow research, no pressure. The opposite of every brokerage's URGENT/HOT/NEW vocabulary.
Modern.manifesto: Real estate runs on urgency. New listing! Just hit market! Three offers already! We started Home Later because the urgency is mostly manufactured and the decision is mostly not. The right house is rarely the one you can see today. Most of our work is the year before the purchase. We are happy to be the friend you talk to for twelve months before you actually buy anything.
Modern.industrySummary: Brokerages compete on listings and speed. There is a smaller opening on the buyer side — a brand that markets to the eighteen months before the purchase and treats long research as the product. Compass-style premium broke ground here; nobody has taken it further.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Compass (compass.com) defines the upscale modern brokerage. Side (side.com) holds the agent-platform position. The Agency (theagencyre.com) sits in the boutique premium slot. We compete on time horizon, not transaction speed — a different axis entirely.
Modern.positioningStatement: Home Later is a brokerage that works on the eighteen-month timeline most buyers actually live on.
Modern.positioningRationale: We bill our patience instead of hiding it. The pre-purchase year is the product: market notes, neighborhood walks, financing prep, off-market intros.

motivations: Want to learn the market before they move.
Want an agent who is not pushing them.
Want to be ready when the right house appears.

messagingPillars.name: The right house, not the next house
messagingPillars.description: We are happy to tell you to wait. Our incentive is the right transaction, not the next one. If we do not have the right house this quarter, the answer is to keep walking.

Luxury.story: Harkness House began as a small advisory above a residential brokerage. The current generation has stayed at the same address. The client list has stayed close to the same size. Some clients have been with the house for three generations of homes.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end residential real estate has been moving toward larger brokerages and bigger marketing. There's a parallel market for small heritage advisory houses serving a few hundred families across generations. Few clients, long relationships, sensitive transactions handled by a single principal.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Knight Frank (knightfrank.com) holds the institutional London peer position. Sotheby's International Realty (sothebysrealty.com) sits at the global tier. The Agency (theagencyre.com) does the design-led luxury middle. We sit smaller and quieter than all of them.

Luxury.positioningStatement: A two-partner brokerage that handles a small number of significant homes per year — personally, slowly, and quietly.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Good Bones is the universal real estate phrase for a property worth restoring: the structure is right, the rest is fixable. The brand names what every honest buyer is actually looking for. Warm, immediately legible, and slightly self-aware.
Creative.manifesto: Most real estate brands sell move-in ready. The staged perfection. The finished surface. We made Good Bones because the most interesting homes aren't the polished ones. They are the houses with the original windows, the unfortunate kitchen, the staircase that creaks. The brand is for the buyers who can see what the house wants to be.
Creative.industrySummary: Real estate branding has been polished, staged, and slightly aspirational. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the imperfect houses that reward the patient buyer.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cottages & Bungalows (cottagesandbungalowsmag.com) holds the heritage-home appreciation peer position. Curbed (curbed.com) does the design-led discovery middle. The Houseblog community sits in the restoration-led peer position. We sit warmer and more honest about the work.
Creative.positioningStatement: A real estate brand for buyers who can see past the carpet.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words that name the small moment everyone in real estate is actually working toward — the keys handed over on the doorstep. We picked the end of the process instead of the beginning. Reads as warm and slightly cinematic.
Creative.manifesto: Most brokerages name themselves after grand things — estates, premier, prestige, summit. We made New Keys because the actual best part of the job is the day the buyer steps inside the empty house and the new keys are in their hand. That is the moment. We named the brand after it.
Creative.industrySummary: Real estate marketing trades in adjectives and aspiration. There is room for a brand that trades in the specific moment of the transaction — the doorstep, the keys, the first night. A brokerage that feels more like a documentary crew than a sales team.
Creative.competitorLandscape: @properties (atproperties.com) holds the modern-brand brokerage slot. Engel & Völkers (engelvoelkers.com) is the European-modern peer. Block Three Sixty (block360.com.au) plays in the warm-creative space. We are sharper and more specific — the moment, not the lifestyle.
Creative.positioningStatement: New Keys is a brokerage that documents the moment a house becomes a home — and works backwards from there.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand is the moment of the handover. Every other piece of the practice — marketing, photography, listing copy — is reverse-engineered from that frame.

messagingPillars.name: The handover frame
messagingPillars.description: Every closed sale ends with a photograph of the keys on the kitchen counter of the empty house, taken by the agent. The image lives on the listing forever.

messagingPillars.name: The first night
messagingPillars.description: We send a small box on move-in day: a candle, a kettle, a folded note from the agent. It is the only marketing we do.

messagingPillars.name: Slow listings
messagingPillars.description: Every listing has a long-form scene-set written by the agent — what the house feels like at 7am, where the light comes from, what the kitchen smells like in winter.

Creative.logoDirection: A small key symbol made from two simple geometric strokes, set beside the wordmark NEW KEYS in a quiet display serif. The key is just suggested, not drawn.

colorPalette.name: Brass
colorPalette.meaning: Primary accent — the color of a new key.

typography.primary: A quiet display serif for headlines and scene-sets.
typography.secondary: A modern grotesque for working type.
typography.rationale: The serif tells the story. The sans does the work.

Creative.brandDescription: New Keys is a brokerage that documents the moment a house becomes a home — and works backwards from there.
Creative.mission: The brand is the moment of the handover. Every other piece of the practice — marketing, photography, listing copy — is reverse-engineered from that frame.
Creative.vision: We named the brand after it.
coreValues: Warm — we are friendly, not formal.
Cinematic — the room sets the mood.
Patient — we play long games, not loud ones.
Specific — generalities are how people avoid commitment.
